title: evp_extra_test fails on NonStop builds in openssl-3.0
body: The openssl-3.0 branch started failing tests on NonStop at or near commit 48fe8d4e53d5572ff77215e3336a1c71b0b4517b. evp_extra_test fails, and I have included the test output and build configuration. Assistance requested.

symptoms_visible: On NonStop, the openssl-3.0 test run fails in evp_extra_test at or near commit 48fe8d4e53d5572ff77215e3336a1c71b0b4517b.
N0.label: N0 NonStop evp_extra_test failure reported

symptoms_visible: The same evp_extra_test failure occurs in all of my NonStop build types, including the normally monitored unthreaded 64-bit build.
dasync.so and the other expected modules exist in the build tree, and the runtime load trace uses the build-tree paths.
N1.label: N1 build scope and module paths established

symptoms_visible: The direct -context run completes all 58 tests and then receives SIGSEGV 11 while exiting.
The backtrace ends in __process_atexit_functions, CRE_TERMINATOR_, exit, and _MAIN; the wrapper reports exit status 139.
N2.label: N2 exit-time SIGSEGV reproduced directly

symptoms_visible: Building with OPENSSL_NO_TRACE produces the same SIGSEGV in the same exit-time location.
Removing the duplicate trace_data_stack declaration compiles, but the exit-time SIGSEGV is unchanged.
N3.label: N3 trace-handler hypotheses ruled out

symptoms_visible: The instrumented middle run prints two registrations of OPENSSL_cleanup and then completes all 58 tests before receiving SIGSEGV; OPENSSL_cleanup is not successfully entered during that failing exit.
On NonStop, the CRE exit list retains an entry after its DLL has unloaded, so a later attempt to call that inaccessible procedure address receives SIGSEGV.
N4.label: N4 duplicate cleanup registration traced

symptoms_visible: The debug branch based on the old 3.0.0 release passes, and the rebased master test also passes, while the current openssl-3.0 branch is where I reproduce the failure; openssl-3.1 is also fine.
N5.label: N5 failure isolated to current openssl-3.0 test composition

symptoms_visible: The change intended to avoid the mixed-linkage exit crash has been merged, but I have not reported a successful NonStop build and test run with the merged change.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix merged without affected-system verification

question_patterns: Does this happen only in the SPT build, or in other NonStop build configurations too?
Which NonStop build variants reproduce the failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It happens in all builds. We normally monitor with the unthreaded 64-bit build, and it happens there too, so this is highly unlikely to be specific to the SPT build.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only happens in the SPT build; the unthreaded 64-bit build passes.
It reproduces in all build types, but I first noticed it in the threaded build.

question_patterns: Is dasync.so listed in MODULES, and which dynamic modules were actually built?
Can you print the engine environment value and the paths passed to dlopen during the test?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The top-level Makefile lists engines/dasync.so, and dasync.so, ossltest.so, the legacy provider and the other expected modules are built. OPENSSL_ENGINE points to my build-tree engines directory. With a printf in dlopen I get ../../providers/fips.so, /home/<user>/.jenkins/workspace/OpenSSL-3.0_Monitor/engines/dasync.so, and /home/<user>/.jenkins/workspace/OpenSSL-3.0_Monitor/providers/legacy.so.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: dasync.so is absent from MODULES and was never produced in the build tree.
The same modules are built under a different Jenkins workspace path, and dlopen uses that build-tree path.

edges.comment: Reporter c1 and c6-c9: the issue affects all of the reporter's NonStop build variants. The initial suspicion that a nonexistent or globally qualified dasync.so caused the failure was retracted after direct dlopen tracing showed the expected build-tree paths.

question_patterns: Can you run evp_extra_test -context directly without the Perl test-harness post-processing and report its raw exit behavior?
Please run the failing test command alone and capture its final output or core backtrace.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The direct -context run reaches ok 57 and ok 58, then receives non-deferrable signal SIGSEGV number 11. The wrapper reports '../../util/wrap.pl ../../test/evp_extra_test -context => 139'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The direct run exits normally with status 0 after the final test.
The same direct run exits 139, but under a different process number.

question_patterns: What does the backtrace show at the point of the signal?
Can you capture the stack when the direct run receives SIGSEGV?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The backtrace is __process_atexit_functions, CRE_TERMINATOR_, exit, then _MAIN. The tests themselves ran without failures before the SIGSEGV.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The stack points into a cipher operation before the final test completes, not into process exit handling.

edges.comment: Reporter c16-c18 after participant1 c15: the requested direct run establishes that the harness's 139 result is an exit-time SIGSEGV after successful test execution. The raw command result and backtrace are user-produced measurements.

question_patterns: Can you build with OPENSSL_NO_TRACE and report whether the exit-time crash changes?
As a sanity check, please disable trace support at build time and rerun the test.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Building with OPENSSL_NO_TRACE did not change the outcome at all. I get the same SIGSEGV in the same place.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With OPENSSL_NO_TRACE the test exits normally and the SIGSEGV disappears.

question_patterns: Can you remove the duplicate trace_data_stack declaration, rebuild, and report the result?
Please test the proposed testutil_init cleanup and tell me whether exit behavior changes.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Removing the duplicate declaration of trace_data_stack compiled fine, but I still had the same problem.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Removing the duplicate declaration eliminates the crash.

edges.comment: Reporter c22-c24: both handler-directed build probes leave the same observable SIGSEGV. They are measurements, not persistent fixes or solution edges.

question_patterns: Can you instrument the cleanup registration and callback entry points and paste the resulting sequence?
Please print when the exit handlers are registered and entered, then rerun the failing middle invocation.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In the failing middle run I see 'Enter ossl_init_register_atexit(OPENSSL_cleanup)' and its exit twice. The run then reaches ok 58 and receives SIGSEGV. I do not see OPENSSL_cleanup successfully entered for that failing exit.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing run registers OPENSSL_cleanup only once, enters and exits it successfully, and crashes later in unrelated shutdown code.
The same two registrations appear with extra unrelated logging between them.

edges.comment: Reporter c28-c34: requested instrumentation supplies the registration sequence. In the same response chain, the experienced NonStop reporter explains the CRE behavior and the static-versus-DLL RUN_ONCE duplication based on the previously encountered #17059/#17345 class of failures; those unprompted facts enter N4.volunteered_info.

question_patterns: Can you test the debug branch against the relevant current branches and report which runs pass or fail?
Does the instrumented build reproduce on the affected maintenance branch, and how do the other maintained branches behave?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The first debug branch passed because it was based on the old 3.0.0 release. After it was rebased, the master build at 07c1fbab0b also passed. The break I am reporting is on openssl-3.0, and openssl-3.1 is fine.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The crash reproduces identically on current master, openssl-3.1, and openssl-3.0.
The old release and openssl-3.1 pass, while only the current openssl-3.0 maintenance branch fails.

edges.comment: Reporter c34-c40, with participant2 c35 correcting the first debug branch's base: the old 3.0.0 and current master observations cannot verify the affected openssl-3.0 case. The branch comparison remains raw test output rather than a fix conclusion.

solution.intent: Avoid loading a second dynamically linked libcrypto instance in evp_extra_test by statically linking the legacy provider into that test, preventing duplicate exit-handler registration across the static and DLL copies; then have the reporter verify the merged change on the affected openssl-3.0 NonStop build.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the same test-linkage pattern previously used for the encoder test: statically link the legacy provider into evp_extra_test so it does not load a second libcrypto copy whose separate RUN_ONCE state registers another OPENSSL_cleanup callback. A corrective change was merged, but a successful reporter retest on NonStop was not posted.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter established the two registrations, the distinct static/DLL RUN_ONCE state, and the NonStop CRE stale-callback behavior. The maintainers connected that evidence to the legacy provider's dynamic linkage and selected static linkage of the provider into evp_extra_test as the corrective change.

edges.comment: Participants c42-c52 converge on the same mixed-linkage class as the prior test-suite issue, and participant1 describes the proposed static-link change. Reporter c53 begins a full build but never posts its result. Reporter c55 says the issue should close if the replacement change is merged; participant2 c56 reports it merged and closes the issue. No affected-system confirmation appears, so the terminal state records landing without reporter verification.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: evp_extra_test combines a statically linked libcrypto with a dynamically loaded legacy provider linked to libcrypto.so, giving the two libcrypto copies distinct RUN_ONCE state and registering OPENSSL_cleanup more than once.
Must connect the crash to NonStop CRE exit handling: after a DLL unload, the retained atexit entry can refer to an inaccessible procedure address and produce the exit-time SIGSEGV.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the direct exit-139 run, the __process_atexit_functions backtrace, and instrumentation showing two OPENSSL_cleanup registrations after all test cases themselves complete.
Must not treat the engine path or missing dasync.so theory as the resolution; the modules were built and dlopen used the build-tree paths.
Must not present OPENSSL_NO_TRACE or removal of the duplicate trace_data_stack declaration as fixes; both were tested and the same SIGSEGV remained.
The corrective approach must statically link the legacy provider into evp_extra_test to avoid the mixed static/dynamic libcrypto combination.
Must ask the reporter to verify an openssl-3.0 build containing the merged change before declaring the affected NonStop system resolved; the thread contains no successful reporter retest.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical OpenSSL builder and NonStop platform expert; comfortable with Jenkins builds, Makefiles, C test internals, gdb/xInspect, dlopen tracing, exit handlers, static and dynamic linkage, and platform runtime semantics.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, persistent, and evidence-heavy; posts long debugger and test logs, corrects earlier hypotheses explicitly, relates behavior to prior NonStop failures, and challenges explanations that do not fit observed runtime behavior.
